results.title: One person dead, five military personnel injured as Circle demolition turns violent – Regional Minister
results.content: Greater Accra Regional Minister Linda Obenewaa Akweley Ocloo has confirmed that one person has died after a clash between military personnel and some individuals during a demolition exercise at Kwame Nkrumah Circle in Accra. The incident happened along the railway line from Circle towards Agbogbloshie, where structures are being pulled down. Speaking to the media, Madam Ocloo, who is also the Member of Parliament for Shai-Osudoku, said five soldiers were injured and are receiving treatment at the 37 Military Hospital. She said she could not immediately establish the circumstances of the death.

results.title: RE : The claim that the people of Larabanga are intolerant of other religious faiths
results.content: The people of Larabanga deserve better than a sweeping accusation that casts an entire community as religiously intolerant. Such a claim damages reputations, undermines livelihoods and teaches the wider public to view ordinary citizens with suspicion. Any organisation making it must accept the burden of presenting credible evidence and giving those accused a fair hearing. The Alliance of Christian Apologists, Ghana, has called for the removal of the Larabanga Mosque from the new GH¢2 banknote, citing alleged restrictions on other religions within the community. I firmly reject the leap from those allegations to the condemnation of Larabanga’s people and the proposed removal of their historic monument. results.title: ICU petitions Mahama to withdraw NPA Bill over concerns about BOST’s future
results.content: The Industrial and Commercial Workers’ Union (ICU) has petitioned President John Dramani Mahama to withdraw the proposed National Petroleum Authority (NPA) Bill, 2026, warning that some provisions could undermine the financial sustainability and operational independence of BOST Energies Limited. In a petition dated November 24, 2026, and signed by its General Secretary, Morgan Ayawine, the Union called for the Bill to be withdrawn to allow for comprehensive stakeholder engagement. The ICU argues that the proposed legislation could weaken BOST, a state-owned institution established with significant public investment to support petroleum storage, transportation and national fuel security. A major concern is Clause 103 and related provisions that would allow private operators to establish and operate competing inland petroleum depots.

results.title: Women’s Development Bank begins recruitment ahead of March 2027 take-off
results.content: The Women's Development Bank has commenced recruitment of its management and staff as the government steps up preparations to operationalise the institution by the end of March 2027. Recruitment advertisements appeared on pages 14 and 15 of the Wednesday, November 18, edition of the Daily Graphic, according to a post on X by Minister of State in Charge of Government Communications, Felix Kwakye Ofosu. Mr Kwakye Ofosu also shared photographs of the bank's head office in Accra, located opposite the former Ministry of Finance building.

The organisation says although preparing children for a technology-driven society is important, the introduction of AI into classrooms must be guided by evidence, age-appropriate standards and adequate safeguards.
